interpretation: Batch 1 produced no crash, reboot, hang, or new console error. The control and seven cases behaved uniformly: the console stayed associated through the 10-second check and disconnected about 35 seconds after association, consistent with its automatic Test Connection timing. W-06 is the exception: the console disassociated 7.3 seconds after association in the first run and 15.4 seconds in the repeat, both shorter than the 35.4-second control, and re-associated immediately. That is a reproducible behavioral difference, not a memory-safety finding. It may mean the console rejected or reset on the malformed DS Parameter IE, or it may reflect variability in the console's automatic test flow. The batch does not prove that every malformed IE reached the parser; the console can ignore duplicate AP beacons. H-011 remains UNVERIFIED.
authorization: The owner approved the control-only run first, then each case individually (W-01 through W-08), the W-04 retry, the W-C control repeat, and the W-06 repeat. Each approval named the case and the 25-frame bound.
limitations: One console, one adapter, one driver, and channel 1 only.
The console automatically runs Test Connection on each association and fails at the internet step with 2110-3128 because the AP has no NAT; this timing is part of the observed behavior.
The console may ignore duplicate AP beacons, so no case proves that the malformed IE reached the ARM wlan parser or the Wi-Fi firmware parser.
The W-06 timing difference was not reproduced with an identical duration (7.3 s vs 15.4 s); it is a lead, not a deterministic result.
The same-phy monitor does not capture the AP's own frames; transmission is inferred from netlink acceptance and console behavior, not from a monitor capture of the injected beacons.
The first W-04 attempt was inconclusive because it was sent after the console had left; only the retry counts toward the batch.
The two test networks remain saved on the console until the owner removes them.
No crash, hang, or reboot occurred; this is not an exploit or a memory-safety proof.
